claims.claim: Feature support matrix for deletion vectors, column mapping, TIMESTAMP_NTZ and liquid clustering across Spark runtimes, SQL analytics endpoint, Direct Lake and Python notebooks; Runtime 2.0 writes reader 3, writer 7 with deletion vectors; V2 checkpoints, identity columns writing, Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines and Delta 4.x features outside Spark are limitations.

concept_html:
Delta is an open format, so a table written by Databricks can be read by Fabric through a shortcut or Unity Catalog mirroring (lessons C3-L1 and C3-L3). Open does not mean every reader supports every table feature. A table's features decide which Fabric experiences can read it.

From Microsoft Learn's Delta interoperability matrix (updated May 2026):

Feature Spark Runtime 2.0 SQL analytics endpoint Direct Lake Python notebooks
Deletion vectors yes yes yes no
Column mapping, name mode yes yes yes no
Column mapping, id mode yes no yes no
TIMESTAMP_NTZ yes no no yes
Liquid clustering yes yes yes no

Three more limits from the same page:

  • V2 checkpoints: only Spark notebooks and Spark jobs read and write them. The lakehouse and the SQL analytics endpoint do not list such tables correctly.
  • Databricks-only features, such as writing identity columns and Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines tables, are not supported.
  • Newer Delta 4.x features, such as collations and the variant type, work only in Spark notebooks and jobs, not in the SQL endpoint or Direct Lake.

Fabric's own writers differ too. Runtime 2.0 writes new tables at reader version 3 and writer version 7 with deletion vectors on by default. Runtime 1.3 writes reader 1, writer 2.

The practical rule: the table's writer decides which features the table has, and every reader must support all of them. For gold tables that Power BI or T-SQL users read, use timestamps with a time zone (TIMESTAMP) instead of TIMESTAMP_NTZ, avoid column mapping in id mode, and check DESCRIBE DETAIL for the protocol versions and table features before you publish.

title: Delta tables shared between Databricks and Fabric
why_html: A Databricks team stored event times as TIMESTAMP_NTZ in a gold table and shared it with Fabric through a shortcut. Spark in Fabric read it fine. The SQL analytics endpoint and the Direct Lake report did not show the table's time columns, so the Power BI team built a workaround copy with converted columns. One type choice in the writer created a second dataset.
